context:
1. Add optional environment fields to SummaryStats dataclass (os, python, cpus, memory).
2. In ASCIISummaryBox._render_single_metrics(), render a two-column layout when
   environment data is present: left column = metrics, right column = env info,
   separated by a vertical box-drawing char.
3. In _render_comparison_metrics(), apply the same two-column layout.
4. In generate_post_run_summary(), extract system_profile from BenchmarkResults
   and populate the new SummaryStats fields.
5. Graceful fallback: if system_profile is None or terminal is too narrow,
   render the current single-column layout.

Follow existing patterns in summary_box.py for box-drawing characters,
ANSI color handling, and visible-length padding calculations.
description:
The post-run summary box currently renders benchmark metrics (Geo Mean, Total,
Queries, Best, Worst) in a single column with unused whitespace on the right.
Add key system environment details (OS, Python version, CPU count/arch, memory)
as a right-aligned column next to the metrics, giving users immediate context
about the hardware/software configuration that produced the results.

Target layout (single-run):
```
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                   ClickBench on DuckDB (SF 1.0)                   │
├──────────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Geo Mean:  1.6ms             │  OS: Darwin 25.2.0                 │
│ Total:     48.8ms            │  Python: 3.12.11 (uv)              │
│ Queries:   27                │  CPUs: 10 (arm64)                  │
│                              │  Memory: 16 GB                     │
├──────────────────────────────┴─────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Best: Q6 (1.0ms), Q13 (1.0ms), Q15 (1.0ms)                      │
│ Worst: Q19 (4.0ms), Q10 (3.5ms), Q33 (3.0ms)                    │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

The data is already available: BenchmarkResults has a `system_profile` field
(SystemProfile dataclass from benchbox/core/schemas.py) with os_name,
os_version, architecture, cpu_cores_logical, memory_total_gb, python_version.

The summary box is rendered in two places:
- Post-run CLI: generate_post_run_summary() in post_run_summary.py
- MCP charts: generate_chart() with chart_type="summary_box"

anti_patterns.dont: call platform.uname() or psutil at render time
anti_patterns.why: the renderer should be pure and system info should come from the result object

anti_patterns.instead: use options.get_effective_width() and fall back to single-column if too narrow

preserves.behavior: ASCIISummaryBox.render() remains a pure function (no side effects, no I/O)
Box width auto-detection still works; environment column only appears when terminal is wide enough
Existing single-run and comparison summary box layouts still render correctly when system_profile is None
